line.name: Sobremesa Brûlée
line.description: Not on the site - the site's existing 'Sobremesa' entry lists only Cervantes Fino and Short Churchill. Dunbarton's own site treats Brûlée as a distinct marca (product line) rather than a simple wrapper variant of core Sobremesa: it swaps the core recipe's Pennsylvania Seedleaf ligero for more Condega Seco, resulting in a milder, creamier profile (cedar, caramel, coffee notes). NOTE: the Mac photo for this is a generic marketing banner, not a per-vitola product shot, so no single vitola is confirmed by the photo itself - the vitola list below reflects the line's full published lineup per the manufacturer's own site.

research_notes: Two further limited sub-variants exist - 'Brûlée Blue' (stronger, aged) and 'Brûlée Wagashi' (6.25x46, milder) - not added as formal vitola entries since I couldn't confirm exact current availability/specs beyond retailer review mentions; flagging for awareness only. Original Brûlée release year not confirmed from the manufacturer's page.
